faq.title: Good to know
faq.lead: Short answers about paying, files and scanning.

model.q: Static or dynamic: which one do I need?
model.a: A static code has the content built into its pattern and works forever after one payment of {static}. A dynamic code holds a short link you can point somewhere else after printing, for {dynamic}/month for up to {limit} codes.

scan.q: Will my code still scan with a logo and colors?
scan.a: Every change is checked as you design. If the contrast is too low, the colors are inverted or the logo covers too much, we say so and offer a one-tap fix before you pay.

account.q: Do I need an account to design?
account.a: No. Designing and previewing are free. You sign in with Google only when you download, and your design comes with you.

files.a: A sharp PNG for screens and printers and a vector SVG for print shops, for every layout of the code you bought.

again.q: Can I download the files again later?
again.a: Yes. Your codes stay in My QR codes, and you can download them again in any format at no extra cost.

rules.title: How unlocks and limits work
rules.1d: A static credit or monthly unlock opens one QR. All its layouts, PNG and SVG files and repeat downloads use that same unlock.
rules.2d: New static unlocks and included Print Packs refresh on your billing date. Unused ones don’t roll over.
rules.3t: Dynamic slots are live, not monthly
rules.3d: A slot is in use while the code redirects. Pause or delete a Dynamic code to free its slot right away.
rules.4d: Static codes you unlocked stay yours: printed copies keep working and their files stay downloadable. When the paid period ends, Dynamic short links stop redirecting and can’t be downloaded or activated. Your codes are kept.
rules.5d: Your plan stays active while the payment is overdue and Stripe retries it. If it isn’t recovered and the subscription ends, the plan ends as after a cancellation. Once the payment goes through, your plan carries on.

responseNotes.notDynamic: Static codes have no destination: their content is in the pattern.
responseNotes.rateLimited: Over the account’s budget. Wait Retry-After seconds, then send the same request again.
responseNotes.unauthorized: Any key that doesn’t verify gets this answer, before the body is read.
responseNotes.bulk202: Poll GET /v1/jobs/{job_id} or wait for the webhook.
responseNotes.bulk400: No code is created when any item fails.
responseNotes.scans200: Days without scans are included with 0.

overview.title: API for developers
overview.lead: Make HeyQR codes in your own code. Start today with the free npm package; a REST API for Dynamic codes is on the way.

items: Styled QR codes in a browser app: shapes, colors, a logo or short text in the center.
Print-ready SVG and PNG files from a script or a server job.
A scan check before anything is shown or printed: contrast, inverted colors, a logo that covers too much.
Full layouts with frames and captions, the same ones the HeyQR editor exports.

blocks.t: One package, five imports. Use the main entry anywhere; the others are for Node.js or for decoding in the browser.

cells: `decodeSvg`, `decodeImage`, `verifyScan`: read the code back with ZXing
`decodeSvgInBrowser`: the same decoder, from a wasm file you host
`rasterizeSvg` and the verify functions in one import

blocks.t: The package makes static codes: the content is built into the pattern. Dynamic codes with an editable short link and scan counts need a HeyQR plan and come with the REST API.

install.title: Installation
install.lead: Add @heyqr/qr-core to a browser app, a Node.js service or both.

cells: ES modules only (the package is `"type": "module"`). Use `import`, not `require`.
Types ship with the package. No `@types` package needed.
The main entry has no Node.js dependencies and works with any modern bundler.
`/raster` and `/verify` use `@resvg/resvg-js`, a native module with prebuilt binaries for common platforms.
`/verify-browser` loads `zxing_reader.wasm` from a URL you choose, never from a CDN.

blocks.t: Host the decoder for the browser

Only needed for `decodeSvgInBrowser`. Copy the wasm file from the `zxing-wasm` dependency into your public folder and pass its URL. The command finds the file through the package, so it works with npm, pnpm and Yarn.
The file is `zxing-wasm/reader/zxing_reader.wasm` in zxing-wasm 3.1.7, the version the package depends on today. Check it again after upgrading.

quickstart.title: Quick start
quickstart.lead: Encode content, style it, check the scan and get an SVG, in about a minute.

items.title: Encode the content
items.t: `encodePayload` turns a website, Wi-Fi network or contact into the text inside the code.

items.title: Describe the look
items.t: A `QrStyle` sets module shape, corner shapes and colors.

items.title: Check the scan
items.t: `renderQr` returns a scan report with a fix for every problem.

items.title: Get the file
items.t: `renderQrSvg` returns a standalone SVG; in Node.js, `rasterizeSvg` turns it into a PNG.

content.title: Encode content
content.lead: encodePayload turns structured content into the exact text phones expect for each kind of code.

blocks.t: Pass one of nine `QrContent` objects. `QR_CONTENT_TYPES` lists the `type` values.
Contacts become a vCard 3.0, the version phone cameras read most reliably. Empty fields are left out and long lines are folded.
`start` and `end` are local times like `2026-12-05T19:00`. A date without a time, like `2026-12-05`, makes an all-day event.
`parseWebsiteUrl` is the same check the HeyQR editor uses. It rejects spaces, other schemes, credentials and hosts without a dot.

style.title: Style a code
style.lead: A QrStyle describes shapes and colors. Every style is checked against the same scan rules.

blocks.t: `colors` takes four hex colors: `fg` for data modules, `eye` for the corner rings, `eyeIn` for the corner centers and `bg` for the background.
Codes must be darker than their background. A light code on a dark background fails with the `invert` issue even when the contrast is high.
`centerText` puts a label inside the code. It shows the first line, up to 14 characters (`CENTER_TEXT_MAX`); longer text is cut at a whole word with an ellipsis.
`art` draws soft shapes in two tints behind the modules, with an optional faint image. The scan check reads the background as tinted.

logo.title: Logos and icons
logo.lead: Put an image or a 24 × 24 stroke icon in the center. Error correction rises automatically so the code still reads.

cells: Image URL or data URI. Ignored when `iconPath` is set.
A 24 × 24 stroke path, for example a Lucide icon.
Logo width as a share of the code width. Drawn between 0.10 and 0.46 (`CENTER_LOGO_SIZE`).
Icon on a colored rounded tile instead of a plate.
Hex colors for the plate and the icon.

blocks.t: With a logo or center text the code uses error correction H, so it holds a little more than half as much (382 bytes instead of 666). After rendering, `scan.maxLogoSize` is the largest size that still decodes; a larger logo fails with the `logo` issue.

layouts.title: Frames and captions
layouts.lead: composeLayout draws a full layout: a card or frame, the code, a caption and an optional logo, exactly like the HeyQR export.

cells: The code with a caption above or below, or text inside the code
A card with the code above the caption
A card with the code beside the caption
A frame around the code; size comes from `qrSize`

blocks.t: Call `layoutCapacity` before `composeLayout` so content that is too long becomes a message instead of an exception. Pass `{ transparent: true }` as the third argument for a transparent background.

Captions are SVG text. In the browser they use the page’s fonts; when you rasterize in Node.js, pass font files with `fontFiles`, or the machine’s installed fonts are used. The caption fonts cover Latin and Cyrillic.

png.title: Save a PNG
png.lead: rasterizeSvg renders any SVG from the package to a PNG Buffer with resvg.

cells: Output width in pixels. The height follows the SVG.
Print resolution written into the file, so print software opens it at its physical size. Leave it out for screen files.

blocks.t: `pngPixelSize` gives the exact pixel size of a layout: mm layouts at 300, 600 or 1200 dpi (`PNG_DPIS`), px layouts at 1×, 2×, 4× or 8× (`PNG_SCALES`). Sides stay between 64 and 8192 px.
Don’t import `/raster` in browser bundles: resvg is a native Node.js module.

scan.title: Check that it scans
scan.lead: Every render comes with a scan report. In Node.js and the browser you can also decode the result to be sure.

cells: Light code on a dark background
The logo hides too much of the code
The text in the code is too long

blocks.t: The report is rule-based: it checks the exact geometry and colors without decoding. Decode when you need proof.
Nothing leaves the device: the decoder runs locally and never opens the code’s destination.

types.lead: The main types, as they appear in the package.

limits.title: Limits and errors
limits.lead: What the encoder accepts, and what happens when content doesn’t fit.

cells: 666 bytes at error correction M, 382 at H
M, or H with a logo or center text
4 modules on every side, included in `viewBox`

blocks.t: Rendering throws `QrCapacityError` when the content doesn’t fit. It carries sizes, never the content, so it is safe to log.
`decodeSvg`, `decodeImage` and `decodeSvgInBrowser` return `null` when no code can be read. Treat it as a failed check, not an error.

items.q: Does the package send anything to HeyQR?
items.a: No. Encoding, rendering and the scan check run on your machine. The browser decoder loads its wasm file from a URL you host.

items.q: Can I make Dynamic codes with it?
items.a: Not yet. A Dynamic code needs a HeyQR short link, a plan and scan counting on our servers. That comes with the REST API.

items.q: Why does my code with a logo fail?
items.a: A logo raises error correction to H, which lowers capacity, and hides modules. Make the logo smaller than `scan.maxLogoSize` or shorten the content.

items.q: Why is PNG export Node.js only?
items.a: PNGs are rendered with resvg, a native module. In the browser, draw the SVG on a canvas if you need pixels.

items.q: Will the files match the HeyQR editor?
items.a: Yes. The editor preview and the paid export both use `composeLayout`, so the same layout gives the same SVG.

items.q: Can I use it in a commercial product?
items.a: The license is set with the first public release and will be shown here and on npm.

rest.title: REST API
rest.lead: Create codes, change where Dynamic codes point and read scan counts from your server.

restAuth.title: Authentication
restAuth.lead: Every request carries an API key from your HeyQR account.

blocks.t: Not public yet. This page describes the REST API in this build of HeyQR, checked against its routes. It isn’t available on heyqr.me yet, and it stays out of search until it is.

items: Create keys in Account → API keys. A key belongs to your account; every key of the account sees the same codes.
Keys look like `hqk_<lookupId>_<secret>`. The full key is shown once, when you create it; HeyQR keeps only a verifier.
Send the key in the `Authorization` header from your server. Never put it in a URL or in browser code.
A missing, wrong or revoked key gets the same `401 unauthorized`, before the request body is read.

blocks.t: Limits belong to the account: all its keys share them, and accounts don’t affect each other. A window starts with the first request and lasts 60 seconds.

cells: Every request with a valid key

blocks.t: Over a budget the answer is `429 rate_limited` with `Retry-After`, before anything is created, changed or rendered.

restCreate.title: Create a QR code
restCreate.lead: Creates one QR code with its layouts, as a draft of your account. Activation, short links and payment stay in the app.

blocks.t: Not public yet. This page describes the REST API in this build of HeyQR, checked against its routes. It isn’t available on heyqr.me yet, and it stays out of search until it is.

cells: 1–80 characters. The name in My QR codes.
What the code opens. Same shapes as `encodePayload`.
`dynamic` only: where the short link sends people. Defaults to the website address.
1–20 layouts: `name` (1–60), a rendered `layout` and optional `editor` settings.

blocks.t: The body is strict: an unknown field is refused. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (1–255 visible characters, a UUID works) to make retries safe: the same key and request return the original `201`.

restBulk.lead: Creates up to 100 codes in one request. The job runs in the background.

cells: 1–100 codes, each like Create a QR code.
One style for every code in the batch.
Called once when the job finishes.

Change it from the `revision` you read: a destination changed in the app or by another request since then gets `409` and nothing is saved.

cells: The new address, up to 2048 characters. A bare domain becomes https://.
The revision from GET or the last PATCH.

restErrors.title: Errors and rate limits
restErrors.lead: Errors share one shape. Branch on code, never on the message.

blocks.t: Not public yet. This page describes the REST API in this build of HeyQR, checked against its routes. It isn’t available on heyqr.me yet, and it stays out of search until it is.
Every error is `{ "error": { "code", "message", …details } }` with `Cache-Control: no-store`. Messages are for people; codes are stable.

cells: Missing, malformed, wrong or revoked key.
Export of a code that isn’t paid or live; `paymentUrl` opens its Export screen.
The account has the maximum number of drafts.
Not your code or layout, deleted, or missing: one answer for all.
Changed since your revision, or a reused Idempotency-Key.
A rule is broken; `details` names the field.
Over the account’s budget; wait `Retry-After` seconds.

blocks.t: The defaults are 120 requests and 30 exports per minute and account. Refused requests don’t extend the wait.

restSdk.title: TypeScript SDK
restSdk.lead: @heyqr/sdk is a typed client for the REST API, for Node.js 18 and later. It renders nothing: that’s @heyqr/qr-core.

`HeyQrClient` needs an API key, so it runs on a server only. In a browser bundle the package resolves to an entry whose `HeyQrClient` throws a `HeyQrError` of kind `server_only`. For previews in the browser, use `@heyqr/sdk/react`.
